I Love Lucy. The groundbreaking sitcom that premiered on CBS in nineteen fifty-one and ran for six seasons, starring Lucille Ball as the scrappy Lucy Ricardo alongside her real-life husband Desi Arnaz. The show pioneered the multi-camera sitcom format, genuine laugh track, and physical comedy derived from vaudeville, setting the template that shaped television comedy for decades.

Lucy and Ricky Ricardo were a young married couple living in New York City, and the show's humor came from Lucy's schemes to get into show business where her husband worked—schemes that inevitably backfired in elaborate, slapstick fashion. The three-camera format and live audience during filming became the industry standard for sitcoms. What networks copied especially was the genuine laugh track as a response to that live audience.

The show tackled pregnancy and birth on television when Ball was actually pregnant; Lucy Ricardo's pregnancy aired as a major plot point in nineteen fifty-three. One iconic moment everyone remembers is "Job Switching," where Lucy works in a chocolate factory and cannot keep up with the conveyor belt. I Love Lucy reruns have aired continuously for over seventy years and remain widely watched internationally.
